arxiv-2002-00240.title: Molecule Property Prediction and Classification with Graph Hypernetworks
arxiv-2002-00240.creator: Eliya Nachmani, Lior Wolf
arxiv-2002-00240.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Eliya Nachmani, Lior Wolf. Graph neural networks are currently leading the performance charts in learning-based molecule property prediction and classification. Computational chemistry has, therefore, become the a prominent testbed for generic graph neural networks, as well as for specialized message passing methods. In this work, we demonstrate that the replacement of the underlying networks with hypernetworks leads to a boost in performance, obtaining state of the art results in various benchmarks. A major difficulty in the application of hypernetworks is their lack of stability.

arxiv-2103-00352.title: Underproduction: An Approach for Measuring Risk in Open Source Software
arxiv-2103-00352.creator: Kaylea Champion, Benjamin Mako Hill
arxiv-2103-00352.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Kaylea Champion, Benjamin Mako Hill. The widespread adoption of Free/Libre and Open Source Software (FLOSS) means that the ongoing maintenance of many widely used software components relies on the collaborative effort of volunteers who set their own priorities and choose their own tasks. We argue that this has created a new form of risk that we call ‘underproduction’ which occurs when the supply of software engineering labor becomes out of alignment with the demand of people who rely on the software produced.

arxiv-2203-02094.title: LiteTransformerSearch: Training-free Neural Architecture Search for Efficient Language Models
arxiv-2203-02094.creator: Mojan Javaheripi, Gustavo H. de Rosa, Subhabrata Mukherjee, Shital Shah, Tomasz L. Religa, Caio C.T. Mendes, Sebastien Bubeck, Farinaz Koushanfar, Debadeepta Dey, University of California San Diego, Microsoft Research, Microsoft mojan@ucsd.edu, dedey@microsoft.com
arxiv-2203-02094.description: Abstract The Transformer architecture is ubiquitously used as the building block of large-scale autoregressive language models. However, finding architectures with the optimal trade-off between task performance (perplexity) and hardware constraints like peak memory utilization and latency is non-trivial. This is exacerbated by the proliferation of various hardware.

arxiv-2207-12811.title: Thermomagnetic instabilities in Nb films deposited on glass substrates
arxiv-2207-12811.creator: I. Abaloszewa, M. Z. Cieplak, A. Abaloszew
arxiv-2207-12811.description: Abstract In this work, we provide a systematic study of the magnetic field penetration process and avalanche formation in niobium films of different thicknesses deposited on glass substrates. The research was carried out by means of direct visualization of the magnetic flux using magneto-optical imaging.

arxiv-2307-07012.title: CryptoQFL: Quantum Federated Learning on Encrypted Data
arxiv-2307-07012.creator: Cheng Chu, Lei Jiang, Fan Chen
arxiv-2307-07012.description: Abstract Recent advancements in Quantum Neural Networks (QNNs) have demonstrated theoretical and experimental performance superior to their classical counterparts in a wide range of applications. However, existing centralized QNNs cannot solve many real-world problems because collecting large amounts of training data to a common public site is time-consuming and, more importantly, violates data privacy.

arxiv-2508-08698.creator: Zhuohan Wang, Carmine Ventre
arxiv-2508-08698.description: Abstract Modeling limit order books (LOBs) dynamics is a fundamental problem in market microstructure research. In particular, generating high-dimensional volume snapshots with strong temporal and liquidity-dependent patterns remains a challenging task, despite recent work exploring the application of Generative Adversarial Networks to LOBs.

pmc-10521491.title: Disease-preventive behaviors and subjective well-being in the COVID-19 pandemic
pmc-10521491.creator: Matthew Tokson, Hadley Rahrig, Jeffrey D. Green
pmc-10521491.description: BackgroundSafety precautions and activity restrictions were common in the early, pre-vaccine phases of the COVID-19 pandemic. We hypothesized that higher levels of participation in potentially risky social and other activities would be associated with greater life satisfaction and perceived meaning in life. At the same time, prosocial COVID-preventive activities such as mask wearing should enhance life satisfaction.

pmc-10536406.creator: Xuening Zhang, Jie Wang, Qian Zhang, Yan Fan, Hongwei Zhang, Khurshid Ahmad, Hu Hou, Gabriele Rocchetti
pmc-10536406.description: The source and type of collagen are crucial to its application, and both play a decisive role. Collagen was prepared from both tilapia skin and bone and skate skin and cartilage, named as CI-TI-s, CI-TI-b, CI-SK-s, and CII-SK-c, respectively. Types, distributions, structures, and self-assembly of collagen were studied.

pmc-11463091.creator: Xingcheng Yang, Lijun Jiang, Xiaoying Zhang, Juan Peng, Hu Qian, Lifang Huang, Shaolong He, Zhiqiong Wang, Liting Chen, Yicheng Zhang, Ling Ma, Yuan Chen, Jia Wei
pmc-11463091.description: The role of the compromised immune microenvironment, including immune checkpoints, in myelodysplastic syndromes (MDS) has been identified as critical This study aimed to investigate the expression patterns of immune checkpoints, particularly soluble PD-1/PD-L1 (sPD-1/sPD-L1) as well as PD-1 on effector T cell subsets, and assess their prognostic value and potential regulatory roles in MDS.

pmc-11621965.title: Long‐Term Success of Teeth Undergoing Intentional Replantation: A Report of Two Cases
pmc-11621965.creator: Abdulaziz Bakhsh, Ghada Eisa, Hanen Hodhan, Emna Sakly, Fouad Abduljabbar
pmc-11621965.description: Intentional replantation has been shown to be a viable treatment option for failed endodontic cases with long‐term success rates.Keywords: atraumatic extraction, endodontic treatment failures, intentional reimplantation, root‐end restoration Introduction Intentional tooth replantation (IR) is defined by Grossman as the purposeful removal of a tooth and its reinsertion into the socket almost immediately after sealing the apical foramina [1].

pmc-11740040.title: Predicting prognosis of locally advanced esophageal squamous cell carcinoma through early changes in neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio following neoadjuvant immunochemotherapy
pmc-11740040.creator: Yizhang Chen, Shujie Huang, Rixin Chen, Zihua Lan, Zhen Gao, Zijie Li, Sichao Wang, Yong Tang, Guibin Qiao
pmc-11740040.description: BackgroundThe effectiveness of neoadjuvant immunochemotherapy (NAIC) in locally advanced esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) remains unclear. This study aims to validate the relation between early alterations in neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) and clinical outcomes among individuals diagnosed with locally advanced ESCC undergoing NAIC.

pmc-12539166.title: Efficacy of different pulpotomy procedures in permanent molars with symptomatic irreversible pulpitis: a retrospective study
pmc-12539166.creator: Muhammed Ayhan, Demet Altunbaş, İbrahim Akdeniz
pmc-12539166.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundThis study aimed to retrospectively evaluate the effects of different disinfection and hemostasis procedures on the outcome of mineral trioxide aggregate (MTA) pulpotomy in permanent molars with symptomatic irreversible pulpitis (SIP).MethodsThis retrospective study included patients who had permanent carious molars diagnosed with SIP and treated with MTA pulpotomy under different hemostasis and disinfection procedures (saline, NaOCl, and potassium titanyl phosphate (KTP) laser) by the same operator in the 2-year period.

pmc-12563275.title: Epigenetic Remodeling in Thyroid Cancer: New Dimensions of Targeted Therapy Through lncRNA Modulation
pmc-12563275.creator: Adrian Albulescu, Alina Fudulu, Mirela Antonela Mihaila, Iulia Iancu, Adriana Plesa, Marinela Bostan, Anca Botezatu, Lorelei Irina Brasoveanu, Camelia Mia Hotnog
pmc-12563275.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Thyroid carcinomas are phenotypically heterogeneous malignancies. Advances in molecular and cellular technologies have revealed genetic, epigenetic, and nongenetic factors underlying this heterogeneity. Our study aimed to assess the impact of single and combined treatments with anticancer agents (Carboplatin, Doxorubicin, Paclitaxel, Avastin), natural compounds (Quercetin), and epigenetic modulators (suberoylanilide hydroxamic acid and 5-Azacytidine) on the expression of long noncoding RNAs, methylation regulators, and functional features in the human thyroid cancer cell line K1.

pmc-12570226.title: The impact of sleep duration on the incidence of new-onset chronic kidney disease in community-dwelling adults: a nationwide cohort study
pmc-12570226.creator: Jung-Hwan Kim, Min-Jin Ha, Dong-Woo Choi, Sohee Park
pmc-12570226.description: BackgroundThis research examined the association between sleep duration and new-onset chronic kidney disease (CKD) among community-dwelling middle-aged and elderly individuals in Korea.MethodsThis prospective cohort study utilized data from the Korean Genome and Epidemiology Study (KoGES) from 2001–2002 (baseline) to 2019–2020 (tenth follow-up visit). New-onset CKD was the primary outcome, defined as an estimated glomerular filtration rate <60 mL/min/1.

pmc-12747914.title: Editorial: Moving towards a sustainable and greener dialysis
pmc-12747914.creator: Sabrina Haroon, Andrew Davenport
pmc-12747914.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). placement therapy or slow low-efficiency dialysis. The environmental footprint of dialysis is substantial, primarily attributable to pharmaceuticals, but also to carbon emissions generated by single-use consumables, as well as the consumption of water and electricity. The increasing global demand for dialysis, compounded by a shift toward offering newer, more complex treatments, such as hemodiafiltration and automated peritoneal dialysis (APD), exacerbates these environmental concerns. These modalities necessitate greater consumption of water, electricity, and consumables, thereby amplifying carbon emissions.

pmc-12931782.title: Communal narcissism and internet altruistic behavior of Chinese college student: A moderated mediating effect
pmc-12931782.creator: Zimi Li, Xiangkui Zhang
pmc-12931782.description: This research aimed to examine the relations among communal narcissism, Internet impression management, self-esteem and Internet altruistic behavior. This study measured 700 university students from 3 universities in the Northeast using the Narcissistic Personality Inventory, the Internet Impression Management Scale, the Self-Esteem Scale, and the Internet altruistic Behavior Scale, with 675 effective participants.

pmc-13064126.title: Why do older people not adhere to a healthy lifestyle: a qualitative exploration of perceived barriers among older people living in a low-income and middle-income country setting
pmc-13064126.creator: Vidura Jayasinghe, Ruwan Ferdinando, Chrishantha Abeysena
pmc-13064126.description: ObjectiveTo explore perceived barriers to adhering to a healthy lifestyle among older people living in a Sri Lankan setting.DesignQualitative thematic analysis of in-depth interviews among older people.SettingThe study was conducted in Kalutara district, Sri Lanka.ParticipantsIn total, 28 older people aged between 60 years and 74 years were interviewed.ResultsSix major themes were identified following the analysis.

pmc-13307869.title: Facial Paralysis Treatment and Facial Symmetrization with Botulinum Neurotoxin: A Narrative Review with Illustrative Clinical Cases
pmc-13307869.creator: Monica Renga, Roberta D’Emilio, Giovanni Salti, Selene Mogavero, Marco Papagni, Federico Biglioli, Alessandro Lozza
pmc-13307869.description: Facial paralysis leads to static and dynamic asymmetry, hyperkinesis of the non-paralyzed side, and synkinesis, with major functional and psychosocial consequences for patients. Botulinum neurotoxin serotype A (BoNT-A) injections are an effective therapeutic option since they denervate overactive muscles, thereby reducing hyperkinesis or synkinesis and eventually improving asymmetry.

pmc-13403815.title: Clinical and social burden of migraine in Japanese males: a cross-sectional comparison with females without menstrual migraine
pmc-13403815.creator: Tsubasa Takizawa, Keiko Ihara, Reiko Yoshikawa, Kanae Togo, Takahiro Kitano, Masahiro Iijima
pmc-13403815.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundMigraine is globally more prevalent in females; however, the clinical and social burden among males remains insufficiently characterized. This study aimed to describe the clinical features and social burden of migraine in Japanese males to identify sex-specific migraine profiles.MethodsA cross-sectional, population-based web survey was conducted among Japanese adults aged ≥ 18 years diagnosed with migraine according to modified criteria from the International Classification of Headache Disorders, Third Edition (ICHD-3).
